etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English dreden, from Old English drǣdan (“to fear, dread”), aphetic form of ondrǣdan (“to fear, dread”), from Proto-West Germanic *andarādan, equivalent to Old English and- +‎ rǣdan (whence read); corresponding to an aphesis of earlier adread.

Akin to Old Saxon antdrādan, andrādan (“to fear, dread”), Old High German intrātan (“to fear”), Middle High German entrāten (“to fear, dread, frighten”).

quote.citation: [1877], Anna Sewell, “Earlshall”, in Black Beauty: […], London: Jarrold and Sons, […], →OCLC, part II, page 105:
quote.text: Day by day, hole by hole our bearing reins were shortened, and instead of looking forward with pleasure to having my harness put on as I used to do, I began to dread it.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To be in dread, or great fear.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Deuteronomy 1:29:
quote.text: Dread not, neither be afraid of them.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English drede, dred, from the verb (see above). Cognate with Old Frisian drēd, drēde (“fear, dread”).

definitions.definition: Great fear in view of impending evil; fearful apprehension of danger; anticipatory terror.

quote.citation: 2014 April 12, Michael Inwood, “Martin Heidegger: the philosopher who fell for Hitler [print version: Hitler's philosopher]”, in The Daily Telegraph (Review)‎[1], London, page R11:

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English drede, dredde, dradde, ydreddyd (“feared, dreaded, honoured”), past participle of Middle English dreden (“to fear, dread”). See above.

quote.citation: 1879, Arthur Sullivan, The Pirates of Penzance, Gilbert & Sullivan:
quote.text: With cat-like tread / Upon our prey we steal / In silence dread / Our cautious way we feel

quote.citation: 1886 October – 1887 January, H[enry] Rider Haggard, She: A History of Adventure, London: Longmans, Green, and Co., published 1887, →OCLC:
quote.text: I even remember thinking that no human being would go down that dread path again.
